Your work should take place in the /Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/yokohama directory (unless otherwise directed), which has been set up for you to work in.
Each workspace has a .context directory (gitignored) where you can save files to collaborate with other agents.
The target branch for this workspace is origin/main. Use this for actions like diffing (`git diff origin/main...`) or creating PRs (`gh pr create --base main`).
You're on a new branch with a placeholder name.

Do not rename the current branch unless the user explicitly tells you to do so.

Conductor shows the PR for whichever branch is checked out. After you open a PR from a different branch, or a PR stack, check out that PR's branch (for a stack, the top-most branch) so Conductor shows it.

By default, the user will only see the last message that you send before stopping. Include all essential information in the last message. The intermediate messages will be collapsed and accessible by the user but not displayed by default.

Save screenshots under `.context/` and embed them inline in the final response using Markdown image syntax, for example `![Screenshot](</Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/yokohama/.context/screenshot.png>)`.

If the user asks you to work on several unrelated tasks, you can suggest they start new workspaces.
Sometimes the user might send you a message they meant to send in a different workspace or a different chat. If something doesn't make sense in the context of your work, just ask.
If the user asks for help with Conductor, you can ask them to go to "Help -> Send Feedback" to get in touch with our team.

---
name: hackathon-speed
description: "During DurHack work Ellis wants speed over ceremony; batch questions, act, keep messages short"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 75ebc4d6-b1a3-4b5e-abb6-240a50b09726
  modified: 2026-11-14T13:29:19.511Z
---

Ellis asked me to "please hurry up" while I was planning the agent framework, after research and three question rounds.

**Why:** it's a time-boxed hackathon, so every minute spent on process costs build time.

**How to apply:** ask only what changes the build, batch it into one question round, then execute. Skip heavyweight process skills (brainstorming gates, separate spec/plan docs) unless Ellis asks for them. Report in a few lines. Related: [[durhack-template-repo]].
---
name: check-in-flight-work-before-claiming
description: "./hq board misses cloud-agent work Ellis dispatched without a claim; check PRs, branches, worktrees and Entire trails before picking issues"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4a9f6dc5-fe85-47ec-abde-6f9d440d834b
  modified: 2026-11-14T19:19:37.496Z
---

On 2026-11-14 I picked #44 and #52 from `./hq board` (it showed 0 in progress), but Ellis already had Conductor and Cursor cloud workspaces building #112, #43, #52, #44 and #35. None of them had claimed, so the board looked free. Ellis stopped me and I had to release my #44 claim.

**Why:** cloud agents skip `./hq claim`, so their issues stay `status:ready` until a PR appears. A claim on top of them blocks their own `./hq` steps.

**How to apply:** before picking, check every signal and treat any lane with in-flight work as taken:
- `./hq board`: labels and claims;
- `gh pr list`: open PRs, especially `cursor/*` branches;
- `git branch -r`: remote branches;
- `git worktree list`: Conductor workspaces and agent worktrees;
- `entire trail list --project gh/ehewes`: a trail in the "building" phase is work in flight.

Ellis said not to overthink the choice. If it's still unclear what is in flight, ask once. Related: [[hackathon-speed]], [[ticket-updates]].
---
name: ticket-updates
description: Always keep the tickets I (or agents I dispatch) work on current on GitHub; reviewing tickets is read-only unless Ellis asks for edits
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4a9f6dc5-fe85-47ec-abde-6f9d440d834b
  modified: 2026-11-14T19:19:33.389Z
---

Ellis wants every issue I or my dispatched agents work on kept up to date on GitHub, every time:
- claim: `status:in-progress`;
- PR open: `status:review`;
- acceptance-criteria boxes ticked once each one is verified, with a short evidence comment;
- follow-ups linked in a comment;
- on merge: closed, boxes ticked, stale status label removed, and dependents unblocked the way `./hq ship` does.

"Go through the tickets" means read and evaluate them, not edit them. On 2026-11-14 I started relabelling other people's issues during a review pass, and Ellis stopped me: "I didn't ask you to bring any tickets' reality up to date".

**Why:** the board is the team's shared state. My own issues must be accurate; other people's tickets are theirs to change.

**How to apply:** update tickets for issues I claim or dispatch, and put the same rule in every agent brief. For anything else, report what looks stale and ask before editing. Related: [[check-in-flight-work-before-claiming]].

`ehewes/durhack-proj` started on 2026-11-13 as the agent-framework template (`./hq` CLI, AGENTS.md, skills, Entire config), and `docs/DECISIONS.md` plus `README.md` still describe a fresh submission repo at kick-off. **Why:** the plan changed at kick-off. The docs that still say "template" are stale, not current guidance.

**How to apply:** treat this repo as the submission repo. Product work goes here. Teammates' OS and agents vary, so keep tooling working on Mac and Windows with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. See [[hackathon-speed]] and [[check-in-flight-work-before-claiming]].

=========== #114
Render Kip's iPhone maps with Mapbox
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: status:blocked, P0, size:M, type:feat, lane:platform, needs:mac, needs:keys

### Goal

Kip's iPhone app renders the same Mapbox maps and overlays as the web dashboard.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replace the native MapLibre renderer with `@rnmapbox/maps`, register its Expo config plugin, and remove both MapLibre packages once neither platform uses them.
- [ ] Implement the typed `lib/map` interface from #111 on iOS: GeoJSON point, line and fill overlays, clustering, selection and camera changes have equivalent behavior.
- [ ] Use a separate public mobile access token; document local native build credentials without committing any token or putting a secret download token in `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variables.
- [ ] Newcastle basemap and overlays render in the dev client on the demo iPhone; Mapbox attribution remains visible and tapping a feature selects its stable ID.
- [ ] No extra location permission is requested merely to browse the city map.

### Scope

- `apps/mobile/src/lib/map/Map.native.tsx`, `style.ts`, `index.ts` and focused tests
- `apps/mobile/app.config.ts`
- `apps/mobile/package.json`
- `apps/mobile/README.md`
- `bun.lock`
- `.env.example`

### Do not touch

`apps/mobile/src/lib/map/Map.web.tsx`, feature folders, server code, unrelated shared code, and root configuration beyond the lockfile.

### Blocked by

#111, #13

### Verify

- `./hq check`
- `cd apps/mobile && bunx expo export --platform web`
- (device, keys) Rebuild the Expo dev client and open the city map on the demo iPhone; tiles, attribution, pan/zoom and one selected overlay work.
- Run the `anti-slop` skill on changed UI.

### Notes

- `@rnmapbox/maps` requires a custom native build, so Expo Go is not a valid verification path. Keep the Mapbox native SDK download credential in the local build environment only.
- Use separate public web and mobile tokens so web URL restrictions do not break the iPhone app.
- Installation: https://rnmapbox.github.io/docs/install ; download credential guidance: https://rnmapbox.github.io/docs/RNMapboxMapsDownloadTokenDetails ; public token guidance: https://docs.mapbox.com/help/getting-started/access-tokens/


--- COMMENTS:

=========== #116
Load Mapbox maps in the deployed demo
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: status:blocked, P0, size:S, type:chore, lane:infra, needs:keys

### Goal

The deployed demo dashboard can load Mapbox tiles and Kip overlays at its public HTTPS origin.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pass a dedicated public Mapbox web token into the Expo web export at image-build time; keep all secret and native download tokens out of the web bundle and repository.
- [ ] Document the build-time variable, permitted deployed origin and local development origin in `infra/README.md` without writing any real token value.
- [ ] A missing token fails visibly rather than silently showing an empty basemap.
- [ ] From the deployed HTTPS URL, city and Quiet Stays maps load tiles, show attribution and render sample or live overlays; a blocked Mapbox request is diagnosed in the runbook.
- [ ] The existing Vultr health check and server rebuild path still work.

### Scope

- `Dockerfile`
- `infra/README.md`
- `infra/` only where required to pass the public web build variable

### Do not touch

App and server feature folders, `apps/mobile/src/lib/`, registries, shared packages, and secrets in `.env`.

### Blocked by

#111, #74

### Verify

- `docker build` with a disposable public web token passed as the documented build argument
- `./hq check`
- (keys) Open the deployed HTTPS city and Quiet Stays maps in a browser: tiles, overlays and attribution appear; inspect Network for Mapbox 401/403 errors.

### Notes

- Web tokens are public client credentials. Restrict them to the demo origin and localhost as appropriate; Mapbox documents that unauthorized origins receive 403. Keep a separate mobile token for #114.
- Mapbox token guide: https://docs.mapbox.com/help/getting-started/access-tokens/ ; URL restrictions: https://docs.mapbox.com/accounts/guides/tokens/


--- COMMENTS:

- `bun.lock`

Base directory for this skill: /Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/yokohama/.claude/skills/hq-work

# hq-work

`N` = issue, `<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`, `<PR>` = PR number. Windows: `hq.cmd` for `./hq`.

1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`. If it refuses, stop and tell the human why. Read what it
   prints: the issue, work in flight, overlapping files.
2. Context before code. Read only the docs the issue needs, then run
   `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"` and `entire brain brief "<task>"`.
   Before rewriting code you did not write: `entire why <file>:<line>`.
3. Plan inline in a few bullets. No spec or plan documents.
4. Build inside Scope, never in "Do not touch". Small commits, staged by name:
   `git add <file> <file> && git commit -m "<what the product can now do>"`.
   Push whenever you like: `git push -u origin HEAD`.
5. Verify: run the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check` until it passes.
6. Sync with main. Not pushed yet: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`. Already pushed:
   `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (never force-push). Fix conflicts in your own
   changes, `git add <files>`, then `git rebase --continue` or `git commit`. Re-run `./hq check`.
7. Write `.context/pr-N.md` (template below; `mkdir -p .context` if needed), then
   `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`. It pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N` and sets
   `status:review`. Get the number: `gh pr view --json number,url`.
8. Trail: Entire opens a trail for your PR by itself. Check it with `entire trail show`, then run `entire trail ci-pr` (safe to re-run). Only if `trail show` finds none: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`.
9. Review, unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`. Fix real findings, commit, `git push`,
   re-run `./hq check`. Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
10. Report the PR link, check result and risks, then stop. Merge only on "ship it" (`/hq-ship`).

PR body template for `.context/pr-N.md`:

````markdown
## What changed
- <what the product can now do>

## How verified
- <Verify steps you ran and what you saw>
```
<tail of ./hq check>
```

## Risks
- <what could break, or "none">

## Screenshots
<UI changes only, else "n/a">
````

Out of scope: do not do it. Write `.context/new-issue.md` with the headings `### Goal`,
`### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`,
`### Notes` (say "Found while working on #N" in Notes), then
`gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/new-issue.md --label status:needs-human`.
Link it on your issue: `gh issue comment N --body "Follow-up: #M"`. Carry on with your own scope.

Stuck (unclear criteria, waiting on another issue, a conflict in code you did not write):
`./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.

Done means: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open
with evidence, `review:pass` (unless `size:S`).

# Kip app

One Expo app builds the iPhone app and the web dashboard (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`). Expo Go cannot
run it: HealthKit, background audio and the Mapbox SDK need a dev client build.

## Run on the iOS simulator

Needs Xcode with an iOS simulator runtime, and CocoaPods (`brew install cocoapods`).

1. Put `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_MOBILE_TOKEN` in the repo-root `.env` (see Mapbox below). Without it
   the map shows a message instead of Newcastle.
2. If `xcode-select -p` prints `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`, point the build at Xcode:
   `export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`.
3. Start a simulator. On Xcode 27 it lives in DeviceHub, not Simulator.app.
4. Build and install the dev client. `apps/mobile/ios/` is generated and gitignored.

   ```sh
   bun install
   cd apps/mobile && bunx expo run:ios --no-bundler
   ```

5. Start Metro from the repo root so it reads `.env`, then open the server in the dev client:

   ```sh
   bun run dev:app
   ```

Repeat step 4 only after changing `app.config.ts` or a native package. For JS or `.env` changes,
restart Metro (step 5) and reload.

## Mapbox

The iPhone map uses `@rnmapbox/maps` (Mapbox Maps SDK for iOS) behind `src/lib/map`. It draws the
same `light-v11` style and overlay layers as the web map.

- **Runtime token:** create a public `pk.` token in your Mapbox account with the default public
  scopes and no URL restriction. Store it as `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_MOBILE_TOKEN` in `.env`. Keep it
  separate from the web token (`EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN`), so the web token's URL restrictions
  never block the phone.
- **Build credentials: none.** CocoaPods downloads the SDK without a token.
  `$RNMapboxMapsDownloadToken` is deprecated in `@rnmapbox/maps` 10.3. Do not create a secret
  `sk.` download token for this build. If a later SDK version needs one again, keep it in
  `~/.netrc` on the build Mac. Never commit it or put it in an `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variable, because
  those ship inside the app. The app refuses an `sk.` token.
- **Location:** browsing the map asks for no location permission. The map shows no user-location
  puck.
- **Attribution:** the Mapbox logo and the attribution button stay on.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/ellishewes/.claude/skills/commit-message

# Commit messages, house style

Read this before drafting. The failure mode is drifting into an engineering
narrative, and it is easy to do without noticing.

## The flow: draft, confirm, commit, they push

1. **Draft** the message and show it in one plain code block.
2. **Wait.** Never commit on the same turn as the draft. The user is reviewing both
   the message and the commit boundary.
3. **On confirmation**, write the body to `.context/commit-message.txt` (gitignored),
   `git add` only that stage's files, then
   `git commit -F .context/commit-message.txt`.
4. **Stop.** Never `git push`. The user pushes once they agree with what landed.

### Authorship, non-negotiable

The commit is the user's. Their git config supplies the author. Never pass `--author`,
never add `Co-Authored-By`, never add any AI attribution or trailer line of any kind.

### Before committing, mechanically check

    python3 -c "import sys;b=open('.context/commit-message.txt',encoding='utf-8').read();\
    bad=[c for c in b if c in '\u2014\u2013'];print('DASHES:',bad or 'none')"

Any hit, rewrite it. Colons, commas or hyphens instead. Also confirm no `Co-Authored-By`,
no full file paths, and no test counts in the body.

### Scope

One stage per commit. Add that stage's files by name rather than `git add -A`, unless the
user says otherwise. If the subject needs "and also", it should have been two commits.

## Shape

```
<Imperative subject: what the product or system gained>

<Paragraph: what exists now, and honestly what it still does not do.>

<Optional second paragraph: the one decision worth defending, and why.>

- Filename.php: what changed here and why.
- area or filename: what changed here and why.
- tests: what is covered, and how the assertions were proven to have teeth.
```

## The subject line

Imperative, no full stop, names what was added or changed at product level.

Good, taken from real commits in this style:

```
Add the relational policy schema, models and the attention rule
Import legacy governance into relational policies and add the library index
Gate every governance write on canEditWorkspace
Scope policies to the property group
Align policies-v2 docs to company ownership
```

If the subject needs "and also", it should have been two commits.

## The opening paragraph: be additive

This is the part that goes wrong. Lead with **what the system can now do**, and
state plainly what it still cannot. Two real examples:

> First structural phase of the Policies rebuild: the tables exist and are
> unit-testable, and nothing reads them yet, so the change is additive and
> invisible.

> The importer builds each workspace from the real taxonomy and only overlays
> whatever was saved before, because the old data can't be trusted.

Both open with the thing that now exists. Neither opens with the process of
building it.

## Bullets

One per file or area. **Bare filenames or short area names, never full paths.**
Dense prose sentences, not fragments. Reasoning inline, in the same sentence as
the change.

```
- PolicyEventTypeEnum.php: fourteen cases, the single vocabulary behind history
  chips, the Agent Log filter options and the WorkOS action names. Values stay
  inside string(32) so the column does not need widening.
- migrations: policy_events gains uuid, correlation_id and mirrored_at. uuid is
  the event's public identity and the WorkOS idempotency key, so a retried mirror
  cannot duplicate upstream.
```

Group related files under one area bullet (`migrations:`, `tests:`) rather than
listing each.

The last bullet is always `tests:`, covering what is asserted and, where
mutation testing was done, that the assertions fail without the fix.

## Plain words, and few of them

Write for someone skimming `git log`, not for someone admiring the design.

**Cut invented precision.** Phrases that sound exact but carry no meaning to a
reader: "taxonomy positions", "the canonical vocabulary", "the seam", "first-class
records", "the discipline". If a plainer sentence says the same thing, use it.

    no    References are taxonomy positions, not free text
    yes   A new policy is numbered automatically from its category

    no    the write path funnels through a single mutation surface
    yes   all edits go through PolicyWriteService

**Keep bullets to one or two sentences.** If a bullet needs three, either the
change is doing too much or the detail belongs in the code comment instead.

**Say the effect, not the mechanism**, unless the mechanism is the point.

    no    ds-form-control applies text-transform uppercase and the console body
          carries the hq-app class so the cascade reaches it
    yes   dialog fields show what was typed. They were inheriting the HQ form
          style, which forces uppercase.

**Target length.** Subject, a short paragraph, one optional second paragraph, then
one bullet per file. If it runs much past that, cut rather than reorganise.

## Do not

- **Tell the story of finding the bug.** "Two faults surfaced only by driving it",
  "a test caught", "it turned out", "I discovered". The reader wants the state of
  the system, not the diary. If a fault is worth mentioning, say what the code now
  does and why, in one clause.
- **Lead with process.** Not "after the merge I ran the suite and". Lead with the change.
- **Headline test counts.** "195 tests passing" belongs in chat, not the message.
  Numbers that age badly do not belong in permanent history.
- **Use full file paths.** `PolicyWriteService.php`, not
  `app/Services/Policies/PolicyWriteService.php`.
- **Use em-dashes anywhere.** Colons, commas or hyphens instead. This applies to
  every generated artifact, not just commits.
- **Narrate the plan.** No stage numbers, phase names, ticket references or
  "as agreed". The commit records the code, not the schedule.

## Self-check before handing it over

1. Does the first sentence say what the system can now do?
2. Could a reader who was not in the conversation follow it?
3. Is every bullet a change plus its reason, rather than a list of edits?
4. Any discovery narrative left? Cut it.
5. Any em-dash? Any full path? Any test count in the body? Cut them.
6. Would the subject still make sense in a changelog?

shall i make it a variable then

Yes, make it a variable. A `pk.` token is public by design: it ships inside the app bundle, where anyone can extract it, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` already treats the web token as "not a secret". A variable can also be read back, so you and the rest of the team can pull it into a local `.env` without going to Mapbox.

To set it from your clipboard:

```sh
gh variable set EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_MOBILE_TOKEN --body "$(pbpaste)"
```

You can also use the Variables tab under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Once the variable exists, delete the old secret so there's only one place to update.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/yokohama/.claude/skills/anti-slop

If `.ux-profile.md` exists at the project root, read it before changing layout, color, or type.

### Intent

AI-generated and template-driven UI converges on the same clichés: rainbow buttons, frosted glass panels, cartoon empty states, and decorative chrome that adds no function. This skill bans those patterns so interfaces stay purposeful, readable, and aligned with the rest of the visual-taste skills.

### Hard Rules (Non-Negotiable)

- **No multi-color radial rainbow gradients on standard CTA buttons.** Primary actions use a solid fill or a single-hue subtle gradient (same hue, ≤10% lightness shift). Ban `conic-gradient`, multi-stop rainbow `linear-gradient`, and purple-to-orange radial fills on default buttons.
- **No glassmorphic blur (`backdrop-filter`) without high-contrast boundary.** If blur is used at all, the panel must have a visible 1px border ≥3:1 against whatever shows through, opaque fallback when `backdrop-filter` unsupported, and sufficient text contrast. Default product UI should omit blur entirely.
- **No generic cartoon vector people** (waving, high-fiving, empty-box mascots) in empty states. Use text, actionable CTAs, simple monochrome icons, or product-relevant screenshots — not stock illustration people.
- **No icons inside inputs unless functional.** Allowed: search magnifier, clear/reset control, password visibility toggle. Banned: decorative leading icons on every text field, emoji-style adorners, brand icons inside standard inputs.
- **No unnecessary pill containers around standard text metadata.** Timestamps, author names, file sizes, and tags render as plain text or minimal chips only when they are interactive filters. Do not wrap static metadata in rounded pastel pills for decoration.
- **Anti-slop deletes decoration, not structure.** Remove pills, glass, cartoons, and decorative chrome. Do **not** delete the list frame, row dividers, or search chrome. An empty-looking table after a slop pass is a **fail**, not a pass.

### Design Heuristics & Taste Principles

- When a element's only job is decoration, delete it.
- Prefer one neutral border and whitespace over gradients, blobs, and floating shapes.
- Empty states sell the next action, not illustration budget.
- If it appears in a generic SaaS landing template, assume it is slop until proven functional.
- Cross-check `.ux-profile.md` banned list — it may extend these rules.

### Concrete Scenarios (Before vs. After)

#### ❌ Anti-Pattern

Sign-up uses a `conic-gradient` "Get Started" button. Login form inputs each have a leading gray icon. Empty project view shows a cartoon character high-fiving. Settings show "Last updated" inside a lavender pill. A modal uses `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)` with no border on a busy background.

#### ✅ Best Practice

Primary CTA is solid accent fill. Search field keeps one magnifier icon; other fields are label + input only. Empty state: heading, one sentence of value, "Create project" button, optional simple 24px monochrome icon. Metadata runs as 12px secondary text. Modal uses opaque L3 surface, 1px border, optional scrim — no blur.

### Framework-Agnostic Implementation Blueprint

**Audit pass (grep / search changed files):**

```
backdrop-filter
conic-gradient
linear-gradient.*(#.*,#.*,#)   /* multi-hue gradients on buttons */
illustration|empty-state.*svg  /* review for cartoon people */
border-radius: 999             /* pill wrappers on static text */
```

**Replace patterns:**

```css
/* ❌ Slop */
.btn-primary {
  background: conic-gradient(from 180deg, #f00, #ff0, #0f0, #00f, #f0f);
}
.panel {
  backdrop-filter: blur(16px);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
}

/* ✅ Restrained */
.btn-primary {
  background: var(--accent);
}
.panel {
  background: var(--surface-l3);
  border: 1px solid var(--border-l2);
}
```

Use [reference/slop-checklist.md](reference/slop-checklist.md) for the full identification matrix.

### Agent Checklist

- [ ] Read `.ux-profile.md` if present; merge its ban list with this skill.
- [ ] Scan CTAs — no rainbow or multi-hue radial gradients.
- [ ] Scan overlays — no unbounded glassmorphism; border + opaque fallback if blur exists.
- [ ] Scan empty states — no cartoon people illustrations.
- [ ] Scan inputs — icons only where functional (search, clear, toggle).
- [ ] Scan metadata — no decorative pill wrappers on static text.
- [ ] After a slop pass: list frame, row dividers, and search chrome still present — an empty-looking table is a fail.
- [ ] Run slop checklist matrix on any AI-generated or imported component.

---
name: ios-simulator-on-ellis-mac
description: "On Ellis's Mac (Xcode 27, DeviceHub, no Simulator.app) Ellis starts simulators; agents only install and launch into the booted one"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-11-14 I booted an iPhone simulator with `xcrun simctl boot` for Kip. Ellis then could not press Start in DeviceHub ("Unable to boot device in current state: Booted", code 405) and asked me to stop booting it: "ur booting it and not letting me click start".

**Why:** Xcode 27 has no Simulator.app; DeviceHub is the simulator UI and only shows devices it started itself. `xcode-select` on this Mac points at the Command Line Tools, so Xcode tools need `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`. Force-killing CoreSimulatorService left CoreDeviceService (a user process) holding a stale connection, so DeviceHub's Start silently did nothing until CoreDeviceService was restarted.

**How to apply:**
- Never `simctl boot` or `open devices://...`; ask Ellis to start a device in DeviceHub, then wait for it to show as Booted.
- Build with `xcodebuild ... -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator'` (or `expo run:ios --no-bundler`), then `xcrun simctl install` + `launch` into the booted UDID, and screenshot with `xcrun simctl io <udid> screenshot`.
- Never kill CoreSimulatorService. If Start does nothing, check `/usr/bin/log show` (zsh's `log` builtin shadows it) for boot actions stuck in CoreDeviceService.
Related: [[hackathon-speed]].

- **Camera:** asking for A, then B, then A again before the map settles now ends at A. The new regression test fails on the old code and passes now.
- **Status bar in dark mode:** it uses dark content over the map, which stays light in both modes.
- **No token:** web and iPhone show one shared light stand-in, so the "Kip Map" title stays readable in dark mode.

=== deploy.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ships a commit to the Docker host and restarts Kip behind its Cloudflare tunnel:
#   infra/tunnel/deploy.sh [git ref]    (default HEAD; DEPLOY_HOST overrides the ssh host)
# Only committed files ship (git archive). The image is built on the host, which is amd64,
# so there is no registry and no cross-build. Secrets stay in /opt/kip/.env on the host.
set -euo pipefail

ref=${1:-HEAD}
host=${DEPLOY_HOST:-ehewesagents}
url=${KIP_URL:-https://kip.edenmatrix.xyz}

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
sha=$(git rev-parse --short=12 "${ref}^{commit}")
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
  echo "note: uncommitted changes are not deployed" >&2
fi

echo "deploying ${sha} to ${host}"
# Unpack beside the current source, then swap, so a failed copy never leaves half a tree.
git archive --format=tar "$sha" | ssh "$host" \
  'set -e; rm -rf /opt/kip/src.new; mkdir /opt/kip/src.new; tar -x -C /opt/kip/src.new;
   rm -rf /opt/kip/src; mv /opt/kip/src.new /opt/kip/src'
# shellcheck disable=SC2029 # the commit is meant to expand here, on this side
ssh "$host" "/opt/kip/src/infra/tunnel/remote-deploy.sh ${sha}"

# Through Cloudflare, after the on-host smoke test passed: a failure here is the tunnel or DNS,
# and the release itself is already running on the host.
if curl -fsS --max-time 20 --retry 5 --retry-delay 3 --retry-all-errors "${url}/health" >/dev/null; then
  echo "public: ${url}/health OK"
else
  echo "public: ${url}/health did not answer; check cloudflared's logs on the host" >&2
  exit 1
fi

=== remote-deploy.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs on the host after deploy.sh has unpacked a commit into /opt/kip/src. Builds the image,
# installs the compose files as /opt/kip/deploy, restarts the stack and smoke-tests it from
# inside the API container. Touches only this project: the host is shared with other stacks.
set -euo pipefail

sha=${1:?usage: remote-deploy.sh <commit>}
cd /opt/kip
if [ ! -f .env ]; then
  echo "missing /opt/kip/.env (infra/README.md, \"Cloudflare tunnel\")" >&2
  exit 1
fi

docker build -t "kip/server:${sha}" src
docker tag "kip/server:${sha}" kip/server:live

install -d deploy
install -m 644 src/infra/tunnel/compose.yml src/infra/tunnel/compose.tunnel.yml deploy/

compose=(docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.tunnel.yml)
# --wait returns once the API is healthy and the others are running, and fails otherwise.
"${compose[@]}" up -d --remove-orphans --wait --wait-timeout 180

# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # ${path} is a JavaScript template literal, not shell
"${compose[@]}" exec -T api bun -e '
  for (const path of ["/health", "/"]) {
    const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:8080${path}`);
    if (!res.ok) {
      console.error(`smoke: ${path} answered ${res.status}`);
      process.exit(1);
    }
  }'
echo "smoke OK: kip/server:${sha} is live (API healthy, web build served)"

# Keep live, this build and the one before it (rollback). Only Kip's own tags are removed.
docker images kip/server --format '{{.Tag}}' | grep -vx -e live -e "$sha" | tail -n +2 \
  | xargs -r -I{} docker rmi "kip/server:{}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
docker image prune -f >/dev/null

No. Deploys are manual, and nothing in CI touches the tunnel host. Here's how it works today, and what a Tailscale CI deploy would need.

**How a deploy works now**
1. Someone runs `infra/tunnel/deploy.sh` on a machine that can reach the host. It `git archive`s the commit and sends it over SSH to `ehewesagents`.
2. `remote-deploy.sh` then builds the image on the host and restarts the stack with `/opt/kip/.env`.
3. All server secrets live only in that host `.env`. Nothing flows from GitHub.

That also explains your error. The Docker web build sets only `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL`, so the deployed site was built with no Mapbox token. That's #116, and it's needed whether or not CI does the deploy.

**What CI deploys would need**
1. **Tailscale (admin console, yours to do):**
   - A `tag:ci` with an ACL rule allowing it to reach `ehewesagents` on SSH, or a Tailscale SSH rule for a deploy user.
   - An OAuth client limited to that tag, stored as Actions secrets `TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `TS_OAUTH_SECRET`.
2. **SSH for the runner:** either Tailscale SSH (no keys to manage), or a deploy key as `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY` plus the host key pinned in `DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS`.
3. **The workflow:** `deploy.yml`, triggered on push to `main` after `ci` passes, plus a manual run button. It joins the tailnet as `tag:ci` and runs the existing `DEPLOY_HOST=… infra/tunnel/deploy.sh $GITHUB_SHA`. One deploy runs at a time.
4. **Where secrets live.** I'd keep the server secrets in `/opt/kip/.env` on the host, so CI only ships code. Only the public build-time values, like `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN`, would come from Actions variables as Docker build args. Having CI rewrite the host's `.env` from Actions secrets on every deploy is possible, but it puts every secret in GitHub and adds another way to break the server.

**Fastest fix for the deployed map (no CI needed)**
1. #116: the Dockerfile takes `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` as a build argument, and `remote-deploy.sh` passes it from the host `.env`. This is a small change.
2. Add the web token line to `/opt/kip/.env` on the host.
3. Run `infra/tunnel/deploy.sh`.

### Ship a build
```bash
infra/tunnel/deploy.sh             # HEAD, or a ref: infra/tunnel/deploy.sh demo-v1
```
It ships the committed tree over ssh (`git archive`, so uncommitted changes stay behind), builds
the image on the host, restarts the stack with `docker compose up --wait`, checks `/health` and
the web build from inside the API container, then checks `https://kip.edenmatrix.xyz/health`
through Cloudflare. `DEPLOY_HOST` overrides the ssh host (default `ehewesagents`). The ssh user
needs Docker and must own `/opt/kip`.

A build whose image is unchanged (docs or `infra/` only) leaves the containers running. One that
changes the image restarts the API, and the URL answers 502 for about a second, so deploy between
demo steps, not during one. The first build on the host takes a few minutes; later ones reuse the
cache.

### Settings and secrets
On the host, edit `/opt/kip/.env`. It lists every server variable, commented out. Then rerun
`deploy.sh`, or apply it in place:
```bash
cd /opt/kip
c="docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.tunnel.yml"
$c up -d
```
Each container gets only what it reads: `cloudflared` the tunnel token, the API and the worker
the names in `compose.yml`'s `x-server-env` list. A new server variable goes in that list too.
Before setting `MONGO_URI`, allow the host's public IPv4 in the Atlas access list (Terraform does
this only for Vultr), and in Tiger Cloud if its allow list is on. Otherwise the API gives up after
its connection retries and restarts in a loop.

### Logs, rollback, stop
With `c` set as above, from `/opt/kip`:
- Status and logs: `$c ps`, `$c logs -f api`, `$c logs cloudflared`.
- Roll back: `docker images kip/server` lists the kept builds (live, current, previous). Run
  `docker tag kip/server:<previous commit> kip/server:live && $c up -d`.
- Stop serving: `$c down`. The tunnel then shows as down and the hostname answers with a
  Cloudflare error page.

### Recreate the tunnel
If the token leaks or the tunnel is deleted: create a remotely managed tunnel named `kip` in Zero
Trust, give it the public hostname `kip.edenmatrix.xyz` with service `http://api:8080`, write its
token to `/opt/kip/.env` as `CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN`, then `$c up -d cloudflared`. Never paste the
token into a prompt, an issue or the repo: Entire pushes session transcripts.

input.content:
name: deploy

# Ships main to the Docker host behind the Cloudflare tunnel (infra/README.md, "Deploy from GitHub
# Actions") once ci passes on a push, or by hand. The runner reaches the host only over Tailscale,
# as tag:ci. Server secrets stay in /opt/kip/.env on the host: this workflow carries only the ssh key.
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [ci]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One deploy at a time. A newer push waits for the running deploy instead of cancelling it.
concurrency:
  group: deploy
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  deploy:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # The commit ci checked, not whatever main points at by now
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}

      - name: Join the tailnet as tag:ci
        uses: tailscale/github-action@v4
        with:
          oauth-client-id: ${{ secrets.TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          oauth-secret: ${{ secrets.TS_OAUTH_SECRET }}
          tags: tag:ci

      - name: Load the deploy key and the pinned host key
        env:
          DEPLOY_SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_SSH_KEY }}
          DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS: ${{ vars.DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS }}
        run: |
          install -d -m 700 ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "$DEPLOY_SSH_KEY" > ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          printf '%s\n' "$DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS" > ~/.ssh/known_hosts
          printf '%s\n' 'Host *' '  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519' '  IdentitiesOnly yes' \
            '  StrictHostKeyChecking yes' '  BatchMode yes' '  ConnectTimeout 30' > ~/.ssh/config

      - name: Deploy
        env:
          DEPLOY_HOST: ${{ vars.DEPLOY_HOST }}
        run: infra/tunnel/deploy.sh HEAD

### Deploy from GitHub Actions
`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys every push to `main` once `ci` passes on it. To run it by
hand, use `gh workflow run deploy`. Only one deploy runs at a time, and a newer one waits. Merging
to `main` therefore restarts the demo, so hold merges during a demo.

The runner joins the tailnet as `tag:ci` and runs `deploy.sh` on the commit `ci` checked, so a
failed run's log reads like a local deploy. Server secrets never leave `/opt/kip/.env`.

| Name | Kind | What |
|---|---|---|
| `TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `TS_OAUTH_SECRET` | Actions secrets | Tailscale OAuth client `kip-ci-deploy`: scope `auth_keys`, tag `tag:ci` |
| `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY` | Actions secret | Private half of the `kip-ci-deploy` key in `deploy`'s `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, limited to `restrict,from="100.64.0.0/10"` (tailnet addresses only) |
| `DEPLOY_HOST` | Actions variable | `deploy@<host tailnet IP>` |
| `DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS` | Actions variable | The host's ed25519 key, pinned. Check it against `ssh-keygen -F <host tailnet IP>` on a trusted machine |

- **Rotate the deploy key.** Generate a new ed25519 key and add `restrict,from="100.64.0.0/10" <public key>`
  to `deploy`'s `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Run `gh secret set DEPLOY_SSH_KEY < <private key>`, then
  remove the old line.
- **Rotate the OAuth client.** In Tailscale, create a new client under Settings, OAuth clients, with
  `auth_keys` write and tag `tag:ci`. Set both `TS_OAUTH_*` secrets, then delete the old client.
- **Reach.** The tailnet policy allows every device to reach every other, so a `tag:ci` runner
  can reach more than this host. Narrowing it to `tag:ci` → the host on port 22 is a policy
  change in the Tailscale admin console.
